title: First Opium War
key_facts: War between Qing China and Britain following Chinese suppression of the opium trade
British naval superiority secured victories along the coast and Yangtze River
Concluded with the Treaty of Nanjing (1842)
causes: Lin Zexu's crackdown on opium imports at Canton (Guangzhou)
Trade imbalances and disputes over diplomatic equality and legal jurisdiction
British commercial interests defending opium and access to markets
outcome: Treaty of Nanjing: cession of Hong Kong, indemnities, opening of five treaty ports
Most-favored-nation status and fixed tariffs negotiated later (Treaty of the Bogue)

figures.name: Charles Elliot
figures.role: British Superintendent of Trade in China

impacts: Opened treaty ports and increased Western presence in China
Set the stage for continued foreign demands and the later Second Opium War
Catalyzed internal debates and reforms in the Qing state
